key_insight: A physics-informed hybrid CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of unseen perovskite samples, enabling faster stability assessment.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable way to screen perovskite compositions and processing conditions with fewer and shorter accelerated-aging experiments.
method: Collected 86k+ PL spectra from 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to capture degradation-relevant descriptors.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity and generalize to unseen materials.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a diverse dataset of 167 samples and >86,000 spectra, and states the model outperforms baseline benchmarks on unseen samples.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the physics-based featurization and on how well the training data cover the space of compositions, crystallinities, and stress conditions.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
